cards.front: Chorioretinitis, microcephaly or hydrocephalus, convulsions and intracranial calcification form the classical neonatal tetrad of congenital [___].
cards.context:
The tetrad is how this infection shows itself in a newborn: eye, head growth, seizures and intracranial calcification. One feature on its own does not name it.

The same baby may have a blueberry-muffin rash from cutaneous erythropoiesis. That sign supports the picture but is not required for the tetrad.

Raw or undercooked meat and cat faeces are the transmission routes. The mother may have been asymptomatic.

cards.front: The hypothalamus must release GnRH in [___] to keep LH and FSH secretion going.
cards.context:
The pituitary only answers GnRH that arrives in bursts. A steady GnRH signal desensitises its receptors, so LH and FSH fall after a brief flare.

That is why a long-acting GnRH agonist is used to switch the ovaries off in endometriosis and some cancers.

cards.front: At 28 weeks, a woman has immune anti-D and a D-positive fetus that has never been transfused. Middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity is 1.7 multiples of the gestational median (median 1.0). This finding raises concern for fetal [___].
cards.context:
Anaemia lowers viscosity and increases cerebral flow velocity. The peak systolic velocity is interpreted against gestational age.

This is different from the reduced cerebral vascular resistance of brain sparing in placental insufficiency.

cards.front: First-line medical treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding is the [___], which reduces blood loss by approximately 90% at 12 months.
cards.context:
The levonorgestrel IUD (Mirena) works locally: levonorgestrel atrophies the endometrium directly, unlike oral progestins or the combined pill, which suppress ovulation systemically.

The local action gives the 90% bleeding reduction at 12 months that beats every oral option in head-to-head trials, including tranexamic acid, oral contraceptives, and norethisterone.

The trap is reaching for hysterectomy in a woman who hasn't had a levonorgestrel IUD trial.

cards.front: Neonatal resuscitation adrenaline (HR persistently <[___] despite PPV + compressions): 0.1-0.3 mL/kg of 1:10,000 IV via umbilical venous catheter (UVC).
cards.context:
Adrenaline in neonatal resus is reserved for persistent HR <60 despite effective PPV + chest compressions for ≥30 sec.

Ventilation remains the priority — adrenaline without effective ventilation is futile in respiratory-arrest physiology.

Volume expansion (10 mL/kg saline) for hypovolaemia; glucose only if confirmed hypoglycaemia.

cards.front: Preconception planning should begin [___] months before conception; the five pillars include folate, lifestyle, medication review, chronic disease control, and reproductive carrier screening.
cards.context:
The 3-6 month window matters because highest-risk fetal development precedes a recognised pregnancy. The neural tube closes by day 28 and organogenesis is done by 12 weeks, so optimisation must precede conception.

Five pillars: folate; lifestyle (smoking, alcohol, weight); medication review (switch teratogens: warfarin, ACEi/ARB, methotrexate, isotretinoin); carrier screening (identify carrier couples early).

Plus chronic disease control: diabetes, epilepsy, SLE and thyroid stable BEFORE conception, when first-trimester glycaemia and disease activity set anomaly and miscarriage risk.

cards.front: Pre-eclampsia diagnosis requires hypertension after 20 weeks PLUS new [___] involvement (renal, hepatic, haematological, neurological, pulmonary, or placental).
cards.context:
2018 ISSHP/SOMANZ broadened pre-eclampsia from 'HTN + proteinuria' to 'HTN + ANY new organ involvement' — ~20% of pre-eclampsia has no significant proteinuria but still has organ dysfunction.

Organ systems to screen at every visit after 20 weeks: renal (urinalysis, creatinine), hepatic (LFTs), haematological (FBC, haemolysis film), neurological (visual, headache, hyperreflexia), pulmonary (oedema, dyspnoea).

cards.front: If labour is established and birth is unlikely by 18 hours after membrane rupture, start intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis at [___].
cards.context:
Eighteen hours of rupture is the risk threshold. Waiting until that hour can leave no antibiotic running before the baby is born.

When labour is already established and birth will not occur by 18 hours, the start time is 14 hours after rupture.

cards.front: Initial neonatal CPAP for this indication uses a pressure of 7–8 cmH2O and a gas flow of [___].
cards.context:
A pressure of 5 cmH2O is where CPAP is ceased after stability in an oxygen fraction of 0.21. It is not the pressure used to begin.

The same order leaves an orogastric tube, 6–8F, on free drainage. Oxygen is aimed at a preductal saturation of 92–98% at term, or 90–95% if preterm.

cards.front: PCOS Rotterdam criteria require [___] of 3: oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism (clinical or biochemical), and polycystic ovaries on USS.
cards.context:
PCOS = 2 of 3 Rotterdam criteria: oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism (hirsutism, acne, alopecia, OR raised free testosterone), polycystic ovaries on USS (≥20 follicles per ovary or volume >10 mL).

Downstream risks: endometrial hyperplasia + cancer from unopposed estrogen (cyclic progestogen if anovulatory), insulin resistance + T2DM, CV disease, and subfertility (letrozole first-line).

Assess glycaemic status at diagnosis and repeat every 1-3 years according to diabetes risk. A 75-g OGTT is the most accurate test; fasting glucose or HbA1c are less accurate alternatives when an OGTT cannot be performed.

cards.front: Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pain + adnexal mass; normal Doppler flow does NOT exclude it, because the ovary has a dual blood supply; requires emergency [___] for ovarian salvage.
cards.context:
Ovarian torsion is a surgical emergency — twisting of ovary on its pedicle → ischaemia/necrosis.

Doppler trap: dual blood supply (ovarian artery + uterine artery via ovarian branch) — partial torsion can show preserved Doppler flow despite ischaemia.

Detorsion within 6-8 h usually preserves the ovary; go straight to laparoscopy when suspicion is high.

cards.front: Vitamin K prophylaxis: preferred IM dose 1 mg at birth; if declined, oral regimen is [___] doses over 4 weeks.
cards.context:
VKDB (formerly HDN) affects neonates because the liver doesn't synthesise factors II, VII, IX, X without vitamin K, and breast milk has minimal vitamin K.

IM vitamin K 1 mg at birth — single-dose, near-100% effective, no compliance issues.

cards.front: The ideal fetal presentation is flexed vertex, occiput [___]; the smallest presenting diameter is the suboccipitobregmatic (~9.5 cm).
cards.context:
Full flexion presents the suboccipitobregmatic diameter, about 9.5 cm. Occiput anterior describes the direction of the occiput; flexion describes the head's attitude.

Deflexed vertex presents a larger diameter; persistent brow is particularly obstructive. Fully extended face presents the submentobregmatic diameter, also about 9.5 cm.

Occiput posterior often accompanies deflexion and can prolong labour. Face presentation is not automatically too wide: chin position and labour progress determine whether vaginal birth is possible.

cards.front: From 14 weeks, women who cannot access NIPT are told that the publicly funded option is [___].
cards.context:
NIPT is more accurate after the first trimester, but it has no Medicare rebate. Women who cannot pay or travel still need a screen they can reach.

Second trimester serum screening is that publicly funded option. It may be considered when no earlier screen has been done.

cards.front: In Australia, miscarriage means pregnancy loss before 20 weeks; the most common cause of early miscarriage is fetal [___].
cards.context:
Pooled international data estimate miscarriage in about 15% of recognised pregnancies; this is not an Australian registry estimate. Chromosomal abnormalities cause many early miscarriages.

Further assessment depends on timing, recurrence and clinical findings. Birth-registration rules are separate from this clinical definition.

cards.front:
At 34 weeks, a woman has right-upper-quadrant pain and BP 126/78 mmHg. Film shows schistocytes.

| Test | Result | Normal |
|---|---|---|
| Platelets | 72 × 10⁹/L | 150–400 |
| AST | 180 U/L | 10–35 |
| LDH | 720 U/L | 120–250 |

The most likely syndrome is [___].
cards.context:
Schistocytes with markedly raised AST and falling platelets support HELLP even when blood pressure is normal.

Gestational thrombocytopenia does not explain this combined pattern. Thrombotic microangiopathies and acute fatty liver remain important clinical differentials.

cards.front: Hypertension in pregnancy is SBP ≥140 and/or DBP ≥[___] mmHg on 2 occasions ≥4 h apart (or a single reading ≥160/110).
cards.context:
The pregnancy threshold (140/90) sits below the general adult treatment threshold because mild hypertension matters more here.

Placental perfusion is pressure-dependent, and untreated HTN drives pre-eclampsia, abruption, and IUGR.

Timing reframes the same number. Before 20 weeks, 140/90 is chronic HTN (secondary-cause workup); after 20 weeks it is gestational HTN or pre-eclampsia, triggering an end-organ screen (urinalysis, LFTs, FBC, creatinine).

cards.front: Prolapse treatment follows symptom burden, not POP-Q stage: the main non-surgical treatments are pelvic floor muscle training and a vaginal [___], with surgery if these fail or are declined.
cards.context:
Pelvic organ prolapse is graded by the position of the leading edge relative to the hymen (POP-Q stages 0-IV).

The trap is treating the stage rather than the patient — many women with stage II prolapse (descent within 1 cm of the hymen) are completely asymptomatic.

cards.front: Decelerations that mirror contractions and are caused by fetal head compression are [___] decelerations.
cards.context:
Early decelerations mirror contractions and suggest head compression. Late decelerations begin after the peak, suggesting uteroplacental insufficiency. Variable decelerations vary in shape, often from cord compression.

Recurrent late or concerning variable decelerations need review. Reposition; reduce/stop oxytocin for excessive contractions. IV fluid only for maternal hypotension/hypovolaemia; oxygen only for maternal hypoxaemia.

cards.front: A complete hydatidiform mole is most often karyotype 46,XX with entirely paternal genetic origin. No fetal tissue is present; malignant risk is [___]%.
cards.context:
Complete mole: empty ovum fertilised by sperm that duplicates its DNA; most are 46,XX and entirely paternal, with no fetal tissue.

Compared with partial mole, complete mole has higher βhCG and malignant risk. Manage with suction curette, then βhCG surveillance; plateau or rise means persistent GTN.

cards.front: A woman has thin grey vaginal discharge, a fishy odour and clue cells. Her vaginal flora has shifted towards anaerobes, with loss of the normally dominant genus [___].
cards.context:
Lactobacilli produce lactic acid, maintaining an acidic vaginal environment. Their depletion permits anaerobic overgrowth and the characteristic discharge and odour.

Clue cells are vaginal epithelial cells coated with bacteria; they support bacterial vaginosis rather than candidiasis.

cards.front: Most malignancies of the vulva are [___] carcinomas.
cards.context:
Squamous carcinoma accounts for the great majority of vulval malignancies in both textbooks, whether the figure is put at ninety-five per cent or about ninety.

Melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, and sarcoma are the remainder named beside that majority.

The malignant end of this range is therefore usually squamous, with a short list of rarer cancers beside it.

cards.front: First-line medical treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding is the levonorgestrel IUD, which reduces blood loss by approximately [___]% at 12 months.
cards.context:
The levonorgestrel IUD (Mirena) works locally: levonorgestrel atrophies the endometrium directly, unlike oral progestins or the combined pill, which suppress ovulation systemically.

The local action gives the 90% bleeding reduction at 12 months that beats every oral option in head-to-head trials, including tranexamic acid, oral contraceptives, and norethisterone.

The trap is reaching for hysterectomy in a woman who hasn't had a levonorgestrel IUD trial.

cards.front: Pregnancy tests detect hCG's beta subunit, because its alpha subunit is shared with LH, FSH and [___].
cards.context:
hCG, LH, FSH and TSH share an identical alpha subunit. Each hormone has its own beta subunit, which gives it its identity.

Pregnancy tests therefore measure beta-hCG, so they do not cross-react with LH.
